Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Government of Bojonegoro Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bojonegoro.
3. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Services for Women and Children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 1

Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence

Article 3

The purpose of services and protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of the child occurring in households and or public.

C H A P T E R III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 2

The principles of services and protection for women and children victims of violence are:

1. Respect and recognition of the equal rights and human dignity.
2. Respect for the rights of victims.
3. Justice and gender equality.
4. Non-discrimination.
5. The best interests of the victim.

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both medically, psychologically and legally, as well as to receive guarantees for their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 13

(1) Any person who intentionally does not provide services and protection for women and children so as to cause violence, allows violence to occur, and or does not report and does not provide protection for victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable legislation.

(2) If the Official appointed to provide services and protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable legislation provisions.

Article 14

This Regional Regulation comes into effect on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placement in the Regional Gazette of Bojonegoro Regency.

Enacted in Bojonegoro on 8 September 2011

REGENT OF BOJONEGORO,

NUMBER 10 OF 2011

CONCERNING

SERVICES FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN BOJONEGORO REGENCY

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously pursued, sustainable, directed and ensure the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation, with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, since the Indonesian Government signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, it is obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

Article 2

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims. Paragraph (3)

Gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women;

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Paragraph (4)

Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Paragraph (5)

The best interests of victims means all actions concerning victims undertaken by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, whereby the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 7

(1) The Regent establishes a community service work unit that functions as a facilitator for the Women and Children Service Center (P3A).

(2) P3A (Women and Children Service Center) as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may conduct partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.

(3) Provisions regarding the institutional framework of P3A (Women and Children Service Center) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, P3A and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.

What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal services.

What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 12

(1) The source of funding for the implementation of services and protection for women and children victims of violence carried out by the Regional Apparatus of Bojonegoro Regency as referred to in article 4 is from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bojonegoro Regency.

(2) The source of funding as referred to in paragraph (1) may come from other legitimate sources.

(3) The source of funding for implementation from other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (2), is supervised in accordance with the provisions of the Legislation.

C H A P T E R VIII

SANCTIONS PROVISIONS

Article 11

Assistance is provided by persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A (Women and Children Service Center).

C H A P T E R VII

FINANCING

Article 9

Services and protection for victims are provided free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible and with guaranteed confidentiality.

Article 5

Every victim has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling until the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions both Government and Non-Government.

Article 3

What is meant by "gender-based violence" is action based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Article 10

The P3A management is obligated to provide services and protection in accordance with the principles of services and protection as referred to in Article 9.

ASSISTANCE

Services for Women and Children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both medically, psychologically and legally, as well as to receive guarantees for their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 1

Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, P3A and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.

What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal services.

What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 2

The principles of services and protection for women and children victims of violence are:

1. Respect and recognition of the equal rights and human dignity.
2. Respect for the rights of victims.
3. Justice and gender equality.
4. Non-discrimination.
5. The best interests of the victim.

Article 3

The purpose of services and protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence based on gender and the best interests of the child occurring in households and or public.

Article 5

Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously pursued, sustainable, directed and ensure the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation, with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously pursued, sustainable, directed and ensure the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation, with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, since the Indonesian Government signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, it is obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE ELUCIDATION

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Government of Bojonegoro Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bojonegoro.
3. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Services for Women and Children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 5

Article 12

(2) The source of funding as referred to in paragraph (1) may come from other legitimate sources.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, P3A and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.

What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal services.

What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

Article 13

(1) Any person who intentionally does not provide services and protection for women and children so as to cause violence, allows violence to occur, and or does not report and does not provide protection for victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable legislation.

(2) If the Official appointed to provide services and protection does not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable legislation provisions.

Article 6

In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive assistance both medically, psychologically and legally, as well as to receive guarantees for their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

Article 9

Services and protection for victims are provided free of charge, quickly, safely, with empathy, non-discrimination, easily accessible and with guaranteed confidentiality.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously pursued, sustainable, directed and ensure the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation, with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, since the Indonesian Government signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, it is obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

3. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. 11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 1

5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Services for Women and Children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.

14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be continuously pursued, sustainable, directed and ensure the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation, with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, since the Indonesian Government signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, it is obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, since the Indonesian Government signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on 10 December 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, it is obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the Law is also a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because it constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 4

What is meant by "receiving protection" is receiving protection from individuals, groups or institutions both governmental and non-governmental.

Receiving information about the existence of complaint centers, P3A and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to accompaniment and development of case handling.

What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal services.

What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

CHAPTERV

Part First

Institutional

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Regency Government is the Government of Bojonegoro Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bojonegoro.
3. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Services for Women and Children are actions that must be taken immediately including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security conducted by the community, the police, the prosecution, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Companion is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Women and Children Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as P3A, is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and children, as well as mother and children. 18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
